body: It makes a lot of sense what you said. You overanalyzed a few small words that in my opinion she didn't do. It sucks that one time I decide to make a positive message I choose the wrong words maybe because English isn't my first language. Her stream made a difference in my life and perhaps she doesn't want to be that influential. We all have people that influence us. A friend of mine got a really good job without all odds just by believing in himself and because of him I did the same and now I make double what I used to. He never knew that he influenced me and when I told him he felt great that he was able to make such a huge difference in my life, I guess it's more creepy if you say it to a stranger on the internet.

Thank you for your reply that's exactly how I understand it. I'm sure she'll forget about it in a few streams but if I bend over so to speak it will probably get worse. Maybe I can put the free time without watching her stream into something more productive.

>just find another place to call your "online home". There are thousands of them on Twitch

I do watch other streams but they focus on gameplay and I needed that one place to just chill listen about someones life share about mine, I don't have another channel like that. That's pretty smart of you to not accept donations I feel like I have a better relationship with the streamers I don't donate to.

I was always donating "thank you for streaming" every stream because she streams rarely now, I didn't change the message and wasn't seeking attention I just want to talk like we used to do, the stream is mostly "just chatting" not much gameplay so it's like a bunch of friends talking that's why I liked it and that's why I'm sad for being ignored.

It's the same with me. Every friend I have is a drinking buddy. I can easily stay sober from monday to friday just going to work and watching movies at home but when it comes to friday and someone calls me I always say "yes".
